facts.statement: Lusonectes is an extinct genus of pliosauroid that lived during the Early Jurassic in Portugal.
facts.quote: Lusonectes (meaning "Portuguese swimmer") is an extinct genus of Pliosauroid from the Early Jurassic (Toarcian) São Gião Formation of Coimbra District, Portugal.

facts.statement: The genus is defined by a unique broad triangular parasphenoid cultriform process and a specific combination of skull features.
facts.quote: It is based on a single autapomorphy, a broad triangular parasphenoid cultriform process that is as long as the posterior interpterygoid vacuities, and also on a unique character combination.

facts.statement: Lusonectes possessed slender, conical teeth with circular cross-sections.
facts.quote: Teeth are slender and conical with circular cross-sections; any apparent lack of enamel ornamentation is likely due to preservation rather than a biological trait.

facts.statement: The generic name Lusonectes combines the Latin prefix for Portugal and the Greek word for swimmer.
facts.quote: The generic name is derived from the prefix Luso, from Latin Lusitania referring to Portugal, and nektes ("swimmer" in Greek).

facts.statement: The species name sauvagei honors Henri Émile Sauvage, who first described the holotype.
facts.quote: The specific name honors Henri Émile Sauvage, who was the first person to describe the holotype specimen.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen MG33 was discovered in the 19th century near Alhadas, Portugal, by geologist Paul Choffat and his team.
facts.quote: The holotype, MG33, a partial skull and articulated mandible, was discovered possibly by geologist Paul Choffat and his team during the 19th century within rocks from the São Gião Formation near Alhadas, Coimbra District, Portugal.

facts.statement: Adam S. Smith, Ricardo Araújo, and Octávio Mateus formally named the genus Lusonectes in 2012.
facts.quote: The specimen was described and named by Adam S. Smith, Ricardo Araújo and Octávio Mateus in 2012 as Lusonectes sauvagei.

facts.statement: Lusonectes is the first diagnostic plesiosaur species identified in Portugal.
facts.quote: Lusonectes was described as the first diagnostic plesiosaur species discovered in Portugal to date.

facts.statement: While originally classified as a plesiosaurid, Lusonectes has uncertain affinities with microcleidids or early pliosaurids due to fragmentary fossils.
facts.quote: Originally described as a plesiosaurid, later studies have proposed affinities with microcleidids or early pliosaurids, though its exact position remains uncertain due to the fragmentary nature of the material.

facts.statement: A 2026 study found that Lusonectes' placement varies depending on the phylogenetic analysis method used.
facts.quote: A 2026 phylogenetic reassessment using an updated version of the Benson & Druckenmiller (2014) character matrix recovered varying placements depending on the analytical method.

facts.statement: Some analyses place Lusonectes among early plesiosauroids, while others suggest it is an early-diverging pliosaurid near Thalassiodracon hawkinsii.
facts.quote: Equal-weights parsimony analyses tended to recover it among early plesiosauroids, while implied weighting analyses placed it as an early-diverging pliosaurid, often near Thalassiodracon hawkinsii.

facts.statement: Lusonectes lived during the Toarcian stage of the Early Jurassic in the São Gião Formation of Portugal.
facts.quote: Lusonectes (meaning "Portuguese swimmer") is an extinct genus of Pliosauroid from the Early Jurassic (Toarcian) São Gião Formation of Coimbra District, Portugal.

facts.statement: Lusonectes lived between 184.2 and 174.7 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Toarcian to Toarcian (184.2 to 174.7 million years ago)

facts.statement: Only one fossil occurrence of Lusonectes has been recorded.
The environment where Lusonectes lived experienced periodic oxygen depletion during the Toarcian Oceanic Anoxic Event.
facts.quote: These sediments record a range of shallow to mid-shelf conditions, with evidence of periodic bottom-water oxygen depletion, especially around the Toarcian Oceanic Anoxic Event near the Polymorphum–Levisoni chronozone boundary.

facts.statement: Researchers note that the unstable relationships of early plesiosaurs and poor fossil preservation limit confidence in Lusonectes' precise classification.
facts.quote: The authors noted that early plesiosaur relationships are unstable and that the poor preservation of MG 33 limits confidence in its precise position.

facts.statement: Lusonectes is the only known diagnostic plesiosaur from Portugal to date.
facts.quote: Lusonectes es el único plesiosaurio diagnóstico conocido de Portugal hasta la fecha.
